title: Identity Schema Migration Contract
description: Draft data and migration semantic instance for the historical identity schema migration lineage and authentication-slice identity data-governance boundary. The data assurance slice treats this as the governed identity migration contract for order, checksum immutability, tenant isolation, classification, retention, export, legal hold, deletion request handling, backup/restore evidence expectations, audit/observability correlation, and safe failure handling.
aiGuidance: A committed migration is immutable. Do not rewrite migration semantics to match implementation convenience. Storage and data-governance behaviour must be proven under an authorised proof plan before readiness is claimed. Backup, restore, export, legal-hold, deletion, and retention claims require emitted and collected evidence; generated reports cannot substitute for missing collected evidence.
tenancyIsolation: Tenant identity data must remain tenant-isolated through membership, organisation, tenant resource configuration, user projection, and external identity linkage semantics. Cross-tenant read or write access fails closed unless a separately governed system-bypass context is explicitly authorised outside this authentication slice. Quota-before-write and broader object-storage enforcement are non-applicable to this authentication slice until separately represented.
retention: Identity records are governed as tenant-scoped identity data. Retention, export, legal hold, deletion request handling, backup, restore, and rollback claims remain proof-gated until authorised evidence exists. No destructive deletion or restore drill may be claimed from this instance alone; audit and observability correlation must be preserved for any future data-governance proof.
